faq.q: Why does the liquid rise in a thermometer?
faq.a: Warming makes the liquid's particles move faster and spread out, so the liquid expands. Trapped in the bulb, it can only push up the narrow tube.

faq.q: Why is the tube so narrow?
faq.a: In a narrow tube, a tiny change in the liquid's volume makes a big change in its height, so the thermometer can show small temperature differences.
asks: Why is the thermometer tube thin?

faq.q: What liquid is inside a thermometer?
faq.a: Most are filled with coloured alcohol today. Older ones used mercury, a silvery liquid metal, but it is poisonous, so it has mostly been phased out.

faq.q: Why do you wait before reading a thermometer?
faq.a: Heat takes time to flow in until the thermometer is the same temperature as what it measures. Reading too soon gives the wrong answer.
asks: How long do you leave a thermometer in?

faq.q: What do Celsius and Fahrenheit mean?
faq.a: They are two temperature scales. On the Celsius scale water freezes at 0 and boils at 100; on the Fahrenheit scale it freezes at 32 and boils at 212.
asks: What is the difference between Celsius and Fahrenheit?

facts: On the Celsius scale water freezes at 0 and boils at 100 at sea level; on the Fahrenheit scale those are 32 and 212.
Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit made the first reliable mercury thermometer in 1714.
